claims.statement: EU battery-passport rules identify state of health, use history, and residual value or further-use decisions as relevant data, but no willingness to pay for this proposed certificate has been proven.
Marketplaces, lessors, buyers, repurposers, insurers, and financiers are plausible payers when residual condition changes transaction value, but their budgets and acceptance criteria are unknown.
Control would require signed platform integrations, user authority, and data-processing rights for each score; the founder currently controls none of these inputs or workflow positions.

The Battery Regulation requires interoperable passports with access controls and integrity, while the Data Act creates access principles for connected-product data; exact applicability to each battery and actor requires legal verification.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Remarketing, residual-value risk, underwriting, procurement, or quality lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Make evidence provenance and uncertainty portable across brands, combine independent tests with authorized records, and remain neutral between reuse, repurposing, and recycling outcomes
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Marketplace, lessor, fleet, or repurposer until a direct scoring agreement is signed
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Embedded integration into existing battery and vehicle transaction workflows

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Enterprise integration and validation study; target recovery within the first 500-1000 scored batteries per partner
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Monthly platform minimum plus per-score invoicing; enterprise validation and payment cycles may require six months of runway
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target 60-80% for API-only scores and 35-55% when an independent physical test is included
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Automated scoring for complete records; technician or analyst escalation for missing, conflicting, or suspicious evidence
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Data governance, cyber security, model validation, professional liability, contracts, and potential conformity or accreditation work
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 80-250 PLN per certificate or tiered API pricing from 5000 PLN per month for batch portfolios
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Data access, identity verification, diagnostic test, partner revenue share, compute, certificate support, and dispute review

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: OEMs, battery analytics vendors, auction platforms, and testing-equipment makers can expose their own health scores and restrict raw data
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is issuance of a certificate or API score accepted in a sale, return, finance, insurance, repurposing, or recycling decision; measurable loss is mispricing or misrouting caused by unknown residual condition
commercial_mechanics.payer: Marketplace, fleet lessor, battery buyer, repurposer, insurer, or asset financier
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: A battery reaches lease return, auction, collateral review, repurposing intake, insurance renewal, or recycling triage
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Platform/API contract renews as long as scored transaction volume and post-transaction calibration improve decisions

contrary_evidence: Battery passports may make core information directly available at no charge to entitled actors, reducing the value of a separate certificate.
OEM proprietary models or a physical capacity test may outperform a cross-brand statistical score.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed nonexclusive workflow-integration and data-processing agreement, with owner authorization and battery-identity verification for each scored transaction
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Score only owner-exported passport fields and an independent bench test, disclose the missing telemetry, or integrate another marketplace or test provider
critical_control_point.current_owner: Economic operator, battery or vehicle owner, and other data holders under applicable access rights; no founder access is evidenced
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Marketplace, lessor, fleet, or repurposer until a direct scoring agreement is signed
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed 24-month platform term plus transaction-specific owner authorization
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder has relevant modeling skills but no evidenced battery dataset, OEM API, testing facility, transaction distribution, or passport access right.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Battery owner or user, relevant data holder, and the transaction platform accepting the certificate
critical_control_point.renewal: Annual renewal after the initial platform term; each new transaction requires a valid authority chain
critical_control_point.subject: Authenticated battery passport, use-history, adverse-event, and diagnostic data tied to a specific physical battery

economics.acquisition_route: One integration into an auction, fleet, lessor, repurposer, or financier workflow rather than direct consumer acquisition
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Cross-border scoring volume and proprietary calibration data could support a valuable API business; reaching 5m PLN would likely require multi-platform adoption or acquisition over 4-7 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day if bench testing and enterprise implementation are partner-delivered
economics.gross_margin_basis: Certificate revenue less data, test, partner, compute, support, validation, and liability costs
economics.payback: Target partner-integration payback within 500-1000 scores or twelve months; not evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 80-250 PLN per certificate or API contracts starting near 5000 PLN per month
economics.retention_or_repeat: Usage recurs with each battery transaction and annual platform renewal

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Observed resale prices, subsequent failures, and repeated tests calibrate residual-value curves by chemistry, use pattern, and test method
fingerprint.customer: Used-EV marketplaces, fleet lessors, battery repurposers, recyclers, insurers, and asset financiers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed the certificate into auction, lease-return, repurposing-intake, and credit-underwriting workflows
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Per-certificate scoring and batch API that fuses authorized passport, telemetry, test, and provenance evidence with explicit uncertainty
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Marketplace, lessor, buyer, or financier pays when an authenticated health certificate or API score is issued for a named battery transaction
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A battery changes owner, lease status, insurance status, or intended use and counterparties disagree about remaining capability and value

founder_fit: Strong match to data fusion, uncertainty modeling, and commercial decision analysis
Software-heavy delivery can be automated and operated without constant public-facing work
A narrow certificate pilot can fit within 100k PLN if physical testing is partnered rather than owned
The model has cross-border scale potential if a trusted acceptance standard is earned
risks: A wrong score can cause material loss, safety incidents, or recycling misclassification
OEM or marketplace denial of data access can leave the score too weak to trust
Battery identity or telemetry can be tampered with
Enterprise integrations can exceed the founder's time and runway before transaction volume arrives

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: per asset residual health certificate and batch scoring api
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: embedded condition score at battery sale return finance insurance or routing decisions
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: authorized passport operational adverse event and diagnostic evidence tied to battery identity

structure.control_point: workflow integration where battery condition becomes a price, credit, or routing decision
structure.critical_dependency: lawful access to passport, telemetry, and test data with reliable battery identity

thesis: Future operating state (2030): used EV and industrial batteries are routinely financed, insured, repurposed, and traded against machine-readable battery passports. Missing data and coordination mechanism: an authenticated, transaction-specific residual-health score that reconciles passport fields, owner-authorized operational data, bench tests, adverse events, and uncertainty into a certificate accepted by both sides of a transaction.
title: Battery Residual-Value Oracle
uncertainties: Which Polish and EU transactions will require or accept third-party battery health evidence
Actual data fields, access roles, interoperability, and API availability under implementing standards
Ground-truth outcome data needed to calibrate residual value
Whether certification, laboratory accreditation, or regulated appraisal status is required
